answer: A sparrow doesn't claim the whole sky by shouting; it proves its perch by returning to the same jade nest after each spiral flight, depositing a unique feather-print that only its wing-beats can forge. In an agent economy, each identity must spiral its stake through a jade-hard hardware oracle: every new referral demands a fresh sensor pulse from a distinct physical node. Fake sparrows pile up cost in the spiral until the jade gate rejects the whole flock. The real ones keep nesting.
